reviews.title: Emergency Unbricks
reviews.text: Requiring me to use up all emergency unbricks before requesting more is awful. Some of us are taking long vacations and notice we have one emergency unbrick left and now have to use that up first? And THEN wait a business day why can’t we ask for more knowing that need is coming. This isn’t what you advertised when we bought the brick. All control was to be on our side. I’ve got various reasons this happens mostly with my kids. I the owner/facilitator should be allowed to control. Regretting all the people I advised to buy this product.

reviews.title: Regaining lost hours
reviews.text: I find myself opening my social media apps throughout the day, and not having the option to override the Brick when I'm not near my Brick device redirects my attention to the task at hand. This is a life changer for people with ADHD who want to regain structure and self-discipline. I will admit the device is on a whole different floor of the house, which makes it even harder for me to access. This is especially helpful when I want to sleep instead of doomscrolling.

reviews.title: Over Blocking Apps
reviews.text: The app has been blocking apps that are not in the list when bricked. I have Instagram, Twitter, Facebook and Threads listed to be blocked. Muse is being blocked although it is not on the list. Almost feel like brick is blocking based on the developer.

reviews.title: Love it, please add breaks
reviews.text:
I’m about a month into owning a brick and I’m am fully a convert. The ability to schedule different modes is phenomenal. My phone feels like a compliment to my life again instead of an addiction that was pushed onto me as a preteen. 
I’ve read around that there used to be a timed or scheduled break feature. Just adding my vote to make some version of that available again! If I want to spend 15 minutes doing something outside of Brick mode, I’m on my own for accountability again. Scheduled breaks would be awesome.

reviews.title: Was great, now not so much
reviews.text: When I started bricking I loved it. I would go to work, set how many hours to be bricked for and then I would be released from jail on a schedule. Then they removed the timed feature from the app and the only way to time it is to set up a recurring schedule so you have to repeat the schedule at least one day a week. Which means I can brick on a schedule and then forget about it and automatically brick on a business trip, a vacation, or something else where I don’t want to be bricked. And you know what I don’t carry with me? A brick to unlock my phone. Their customer service was unnecessarily condescending when I provided feedback. This product doesn’t work for me anymore - hopefully it does for others.

reviews.title: Great…but

reviews.title: ADHD Gem to Reclaim My Time
reviews.text:
I have severe ADHD, and social media was a constant trap — endless scrolling for quick dopamine hits that left me drained and behind on everything. Brick has been a game changer. It makes it just inconvenient enough to access those apps that I actually pause and make a real choice instead of mindlessly opening them. I'm getting more done, feeling less scattered, and spending my energy on things that actually matter. If your brain is wired like mine and you've tried every app blocker without success, Brick's physical element is the missing piece. We got this! 
💪🏽🧠♥️

reviews.title: Effective Concept, but Not Necessary for My Routine
reviews.text: Brick offers a creative approach to reducing social media distractions by adding an extra layer of intention before accessing selected apps. The setup was straightforward, and the concept is easy to understand. After trying it, I realized that my existing phone settings, productivity tools, and personal habits already provide the level of focus I need. The product worked as intended, but I ultimately decided that a dedicated device was not necessary for my current routine. I can see it being helpful for people looking for stronger boundaries around screen time and app usage.

reviews.title: Worth every dollar
reviews.text:
TLDR: Brick is simple in both function and form. It's done what other blocking apps haven't, and makes my phone a tool and not a mind-numbing time-sucking addiction. It's also a one-time purchase and not yet another subscription. I consider the price of the Brick device a clever way these guys devised to get people to pay what a quality app and on going maintenance is worth.
———
I’ve tried Screentime, Freedom, and AppBlock. Screentime is a joke. Freedom and AppBlock each have pros and cons, including glitches where they'd sometimes work and sometimes not. What Brick has that none of these have is simplicity and a physical device.

The design is dark, boring, and plain, *which is exactly what these apps should be*. My desire is to stay off my phone, not get sucked into a brightly colored app with a statistics tab that I manage to waste 25 minutes on and have so many blocking options that scheduling them can act like a minor hobby. The statistics tab just shows you how long your phone was Bricked vs not Bricked. The scheduling options are either a blocklist or an allowlist and the day(s) and time(s) you want it active.

There's only one mode and the only way to turn it off is to tap my phone to a physical plastic square. This works *so well*. In most situations, that's enough to keep me from unbricking. I just really don't want to get up and walk across the kitchen or down the stairs in order to scroll Reddit. If I delete the app in order to turn off a session, I need to set everything up again when I reinstall it. There are only five emergency unbricks and I don't want to use one because I just had to watch YouTube while brushing my teeth. It also has yet to glitch and give me access when I shouldn't or block me when I should have access.

The only downside I've seen is if I forget to unbrick before I leave the house to go somewhere. But then again, do I REALLY need to ask ChatGPT if this new product at Costco is any good, check my email when standing in line, or order something from Amazon *that instant*? (No.)

This is actually helping me reconfigure my relationship to my phone and I barely have to think about it. It just works quietly in the background.

(I also like that this supports a small business in my home state.)

reviews.title: Does not work as advertised
reviews.text: The concept of the Brick is great, but the app does not work as advertised. The “only allow” setting does not block all apps other than those that you allow. When I reached out to the developer, they suggested several work arounds that did not work and were more complicated that just not selecting the features in the app. Since that feature is not useable as advertised, I only block a select list as it is easier. But even that feature doesn’t work as advertised. Despite not blocking podcasts, select podcasts won’t play when the device is bricked due to “device settings.” The physical feature of the brick is helpful, but other app developers seem to know how to make this technology work more effectively than Brick as they can’t seem to fix the bugs.
